'''Caldo de queso''' is a traditional queso ([[cheese]]) soup made in places in [[Hermosillo, Sonora]] (north [[Mexico]]).<ref>{{cite web|last1=Arellano|first1=Gustavo|title=Five Sonoran Dishes All Cal-Mex Restaurants Should Incorporate Into Their Menus|url=http://blogs.ocweekly.com/stickaforkinit/2012/04/sonoran_cuisine_caldo_de_queso_poblana_sauce_toritos.php|website=[[OC Weekly]]|access-date=29 June 2015|date=30 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150702192824/http://blogs.ocweekly.com/stickaforkinit/2012/04/sonoran_cuisine_caldo_de_queso_poblana_sauce_toritos.php|archive-date=2 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-08-31 |title=This Potato Soup Is Hiding a Cheesy Surprise |url=https://www.epicurious.com/expert-advice/caldo-de-queso-potato-soup-is-hiding-a-cheesy-surprise-article |access-date=2023-10-06 |website=Epicurious |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Avalos |first=Maricruz |date=2020-09-27 |title=Caldo De Queso: A Delicious Cheese & Potato Soup From Sonora |url=https://www.maricruzavalos.com/caldo-de-queso/ |access-date=2023-10-06 |language=en-US}}</ref>

The soup is made with boiled water, diced [[potatoes]], [[onion]]s, [[tomato]], [[New Mexico chile|green chiles]] and [[oregano]]. [[Tomato puree]] or [[Bouillon cube|dehydrated chicken broth]] may also be added to the mix as condiments.<ref name=":0" />

The cheese is usually added only at the end, once the other ingredients are boiled, to prevent [[gratin]]ation. It is most usually prepared with dices of [[Cheeses of Mexico|queso ranchero]], [[queso fresco]] or [[Cotija cheese|queso cotija]]; the contact with the boiling soup heats the cheese and gives it a gummy, chewable texture; in turn it melts slightly, giving the soup a characteristic flavor.

Caldo de queso is generally accompanied by [[chiltepin]] or [[totopos]] (fried corn tortilla chips).
